content:
Rafael Mendes: need to lock beta cohort for incident-bot v2 for next SRE rotation. goal: small + representative, but not so small we miss issues. who do we want in cohort?

Miles Thornton: proposing SRE primary/secondary rotation only (no broader eng-oncall yet). scope: #incidents + #eng-oncall threads, only when bot is invoked / when it posts context.

Aisha Bello: +1. also suggest limiting by env at first: prod only, but only for Hosted API + routing/control-plane incidents. Dedicated has different dashboards + labels, can add week 2.

Jacob Stein: agree. key is we capture feedback in a structured way or we’ll just get vibes.

Talia Benson: timeline wise: next rotation starts Mon. can we do 1-week beta then retro?

Rafael Mendes: yep. would like to define:
1) cohort
2) what “good” looks like
3) what feedback to capture (and where)

Dylan Brooks: feature flag supports cohort targeting by Slack user + channel allowlist. easiest is: allowlist #incidents and #eng-oncall, plus SRE rotation group for interactive actions.

Devon Price: re: Slack side, we can also limit interactive buttons (expand diff, refresh telemetry) to cohort so we don’t get thundering herd.

Miles Thornton: ok, cohort proposal:
- SRE primary + secondary oncall for Hosted API rotation (the one that covers latency/5xx/streaming)
- SRE secondary for infra capacity (for saturation signals validation)
No platform eng yet.

Sean Gallagher: keep it tight. we want enough incidents to validate the “first 5 mins” improvement but we can’t risk a Slack bot change confusing all responders.

Aisha Bello: can we explicitly exclude Sev0 for first 48h? (or at least have a manual disable step)

Devon Price: we can do: v2 cards only, but also include a “View legacy summary” link + quick disable via feature flag. if Sev0, oncall can flip it off.

Rafael Mendes: ok. who’s on the next Hosted API rotation? (names)

Miles Thornton: next week primary is Jacob, secondary is Aisha (per PagerDuty). following week is Miles + Rafael.

Jacob Stein: correct.

Aisha Bello: yep.

Rafael Mendes: then beta cohort = Jacob + Aisha (week 1), plus Miles + Rafael (week 2) if week 1 stable.

Talia Benson: can we add one “observer” from incident automation to watch threads / collect notes? (Miles already is)

Miles Thornton: i’ll monitor.

Dylan Brooks: for access/perms: config diff card needs bot scope + the SREs need to be in the approved role to click “expand diff”. everyone in cohort already has it.

Aisha Bello: what feedback do we want captured, specifically?

Jacob Stein: minimum:
- Did the bot post within 60s?
- Were all 3 cards present (Deploy / Config diff / Saturation)?
- Any card empty? why? (permissions vs timeouts)
- Were links correct (service/region/time window)?
- Did saturation highlights match reality or cause false alarms?

Miles Thornton: + add “actionability”: did it directly lead to mitigation decision (rollback, reroute, capacity shift) or just extra noise.

Rafael Mendes: i’d like a simple rubric so we can aggregate:
For each incident where v2 posted, drop a 30s rating.

Talia Benson: where do we capture it? google form? slack emoji? linear?

Aisha Bello: emoji is fast but not enough detail. maybe a short template reply in thread + a weekly form for totals.

Dylan Brooks: we can also have incident-bot DM the oncall after an incident resolves: “rate usefulness 1-5 + pick missing items.” but that’s more work.

Devon Price: DM follow-up might be intrusive during the beta. i'd start with manual.

Rafael Mendes: ok: manual template in #eng-sre pinned for beta week. oncall fills for each Sev1/Sev2 (and Sev0 if it happens).

Miles Thornton: template suggestion:
```
Incident link:
Sev:
Service/region:
Bot v2 posted? (Y/N)
Time to post (rough): <1m / 1-3m / >3m
Cards present: Deploy [ ] Config diff [ ] Saturation [ ]
Most useful card:
Any incorrect info? (what)
Any missing info? (what)
Noise level: low / med / high
Degraded mode triggered? (cached/links only) Y/N
Did it change action taken? Y/N + how
```

Aisha Bello: add “SLO link correctness”: did error budget burn links land on right route + window.

Jacob Stein: and “redaction safety”: did we see anything that looked like secrets / tenant-identifying strings in the diff output.

Sean Gallagher: +1. if we see ANY redaction concerns we pause the rollout immediately.

Rafael Mendes: ok adding:
- Redaction concerns? (Y/N) -> page Miles + Marcus if Y

Miles Thornton: agreed. also we should track bot query impact (telemetry query latency). not asking oncall to measure, but we’ll watch dashboards.

Dylan Brooks: i’ll set up a quick metric: `incident_bot.context_generation_ms` + `context_completeness_score` logged per invocation. can share end-of-week.

Aisha Bello: define “context completeness score” explicitly so we’re not handwavy.

Jacob Stein: simplest: 0-3 count of cards with non-empty payloads. bonus point if the dashboard links resolve (200).

Devon Price: links resolving is hard to detect from bot side (we don’t get HTTP from the user click), but we can validate URL generation + params.

Rafael Mendes: keep it 0-3 for beta. we’ll also scan for “link bug” reports via template.

Talia Benson: who will post the pinned template + beta instructions?

Rafael Mendes: i will. also will schedule 20m retro next Fri.

Miles Thornton: operational note: if bot doesn’t respond in 90s, it should post degraded mode w/ cached context + links, not keep spinning.

Devon Price: already in build. degraded message includes: “Telemetry queries timing out; try again” + direct dashboard links.

incident-bot: System message: Feature flag `incident_bot_v2_diagnostics` updated (dry-run): cohort users = Jacob Stein, Aisha Bello; channels = #incidents, #eng-oncall; actions enabled = config_diff_expand, telemetry_refresh; effective at 2025-02-17T19:12:10Z.

Sean Gallagher: great. call it: week 1 cohort Jacob + Aisha, week 2 expand to Miles + Rafael if green. success = fewer “what changed?” messages in first 5 mins + faster mitigate decisions.

Aisha Bello: can we also explicitly say what we’re NOT trying to solve in beta? (e.g., root cause, full postmortem automation)

Rafael Mendes: yes. beta goal is correctness + speed + bounded load. not “bot tells you the answer.”

Jacob Stein: :thumbsup: I’ll fill out the template for every Sev1/Sev2 I touch next week.

Miles Thornton: same. also please drop any weirdness in-thread (empty cards, wrong region) even if you fill template later.

Talia Benson: noted. i’ll add retro agenda: what helped, what was noisy, what to cut before GA.

Dylan Brooks: i’ll stay on standby for quick patches if we see timeouts / rate limits too aggressive.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. i’ll post pinned message + link to template now.
